title: A Prosecutor’s Winning Strategy in the Ahmaud Arbery Case

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin and I'm Mark Ronson and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰，我是马克·朗森，欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一档专注于设计之美及其周边文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl,
sentences.zh: 即使是在我那个黑胶唱片时代的夜店当DJ的时候，

sentences.en: every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you and you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你每晚都要带着300件最珍贵的宝贝去工作，把DJ台变成一个充满50年历史精美文物的流动博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼出品的《重构者》吧。

sentences.en: From New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Madam Foreperson, I understand you have reached a verdict as to each defendant.
sentences.zh: 陪审团长女士，我了解到你们已经对每位被告作出了裁决。

sentences.en: If you can please hand your verdict forms to the sheriff.
sentences.zh: 请将裁决书交给法警。

sentences.en: Today.
sentences.zh: 今天。

sentences.en: We, the jury, find the defendant, Travis McMichael, the defendant, Greg McMichael, and the defendant, William R.
sentences.zh: 我们陪审团认定被告特拉维斯·麦克迈克尔、被告格雷格·麦克迈克尔以及被告威廉·R·

sentences.en: Bryan, guilty.
sentences.zh: 布莱恩，有罪。

sentences.en: Guilty.
sentences.zh: 有罪。

sentences.en: Guilty.
sentences.zh: 有罪。

sentences.en: Guilty.
sentences.zh: 有罪。

sentences.en: The three men who killed Ahmaud Arbery have been found guilty of murder.
sentences.zh: 杀害阿莫德·阿伯里的三名男子被判谋杀罪成立。

sentences.en: The Triggerman, Travis McMichael, his father, Gregory McMichael, and their neighbor, William Roddy Bryan,
sentences.zh: 开枪者特拉维斯·麦克迈克尔、他的父亲格雷戈里·麦克迈克尔，以及他们的邻居威廉·罗迪·布莱恩，

sentences.en: claimed that they suspected Ahmaud Arbery of burglaries in their neighborhood and were attempting to make a citizen's arreSt.
sentences.zh: 声称他们怀疑阿莫德·阿伯里在社区内入室盗窃，并试图进行“公民逮捕”。

sentences.en: I spoke to my colleague, Richard Fawcett, about why the prosecutors chose not to make race the center of a case that many saw as an obvious act of racial violence.
sentences.zh: 我和同事理查德·福塞特聊了聊，探讨为什么检察官选择不把种族问题作为案件的核心，尽管许多人认为这显然是一起种族暴力事件。

sentences.en: It's Monday, November 29th.
sentences.zh: 今天是11月29日，星期一。

sentences.en: Richard, heading into deliberations last week, it was not at all clear what direction the jurors were going to go in with this verdict.
sentences.zh: 理查德，上周进入审议阶段时，陪审团会做出什么样的裁决还完全不明朗。

sentences.en: And I think a lot of that came down to two things.
sentences.zh: 我认为这很大程度上归结为两点。

sentences.en: The first was our sense, as you had told us, that under Georgia's self-defense and citizen's arrest laws, the three defendants in this case would have a relatively strong case.
sentences.zh: 首先是我们的感觉，正如你之前告诉我们的，根据佐治亚州的自卫法和公民逮捕法，本案的三名被告似乎有相当充分的辩护理由。

sentences.en: And the second was the verdict just a few days earlier in the case of Kyle Rittenhouse, where a self-defense argument had prevailed.
sentences.zh: 其次是几天前凯尔·里滕豪斯案的判决，在那起案件中，自卫辩护成功了。

sentences.en: And yet, here the jury overwhelmingly found all three men involved, in this case, guilty of murder.
sentences.zh: 然而，陪审团最终以压倒性多数认定涉案的三名男子谋杀罪成立。

sentences.en: So, help us understand how we got here.
sentences.zh: 那么，请帮我们梳理一下我们是如何走到这一步的。

sentences.en: Well, I think one of the elements of this trial that stood out to many of the people who were watching it from the outside
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为这场审判中，许多场外观察者注意到的一个要素是，

sentences.en: was this key decision by the prosecution team and the lead prosecutor, Linda Donokoski,
sentences.zh: 检方团队和首席检察官琳达·杜尼科斯基做出的关键决定，

sentences.en: that really kind of went against the grain of the broader narrative of the story of the killing of Ahmaud Arbery.
sentences.zh: 这实际上与阿莫德·阿伯里遇害案的整体叙事背道而驰。

sentences.en: To the world at large, and to the people who were following this case closely, it was interesting, but also just tremendously horrible,
sentences.zh: 对于外界和密切关注此案的人来说，这不仅令人关注，而且极其可怕，

sentences.en: because of the way that it echoed some of the very most shameful aspects of Southern history, particularly the extrajudicial killing of Black people at the hands of white people.
sentences.zh: 因为它呼应了美国南方历史上一些最可耻的方面，特别是白人对黑人实施的私刑。

sentences.en: It was white men in two pickup trucks chasing a black man through a largely white subdivision in the Deep South.
sentences.zh: 那是两辆皮卡车里的白人男子，在南方腹地一个以白人为主的社区里追逐一名黑人男子。

sentences.en: And yet, Ms. Donokoski, who is this white prosecutor from Cobb County, who had spent most of her time in the big liberal city of Atlanta, nearly 300 miles away,
sentences.zh: 然而，来自科布县的白人检察官杜尼科斯基女士，她大部分时间都在距离这里近300英里外的大型自由派城市亚特兰大度过，

sentences.en: came down to Glynn County, Georgia, and she decided to really only kind of glancingly touch on race as a motivation
sentences.zh: 她来到佐治亚州格林县，决定在动机方面仅轻描淡写地触及种族问题，

sentences.en: when there were a lot of people who thought that it should have been very central to her argument before the jury.
sentences.zh: 而当时有很多人认为这本应是她在陪审团面前辩论的核心。

sentences.en: So why do you think the prosecutor, Ms. Donokoski, chose this strategy?
sentences.zh: 那么你认为杜尼科斯基检察官为什么选择这种策略？

sentences.en: Well, the biggest piece of it, and a lot of this we're just guessing at her strategy,
sentences.zh: 嗯，最主要的原因——关于她的策略我们大多是在猜测——

sentences.en: was the fact that of the 12 people on the jury, 11 of them were white and one of them was black.
sentences.zh: 是陪审团的12人中，有11人是白人，只有1人是黑人。

sentences.en: And so there's a theory out there that her presentation had to be, you know, kind of custom-tailored to that kind of jury.
sentences.zh: 因此有一种理论认为，她的陈述必须针对这种陪审团进行“量身定制”。

sentences.en: You know, a lot of legal experts will tell you that the racial composition of juries in the United States tends to really matter.
sentences.zh: 你知道，许多法律专家会告诉你，在美国，陪审团的种族构成确实非常重要。

sentences.en: There was a law professor named Paul Butler from Georgetown University who mentioned to me, well, look, you have a case like the Derek Chauvin trial in Minneapolis
sentences.zh: 乔治城大学的法学教授保罗·巴特勒曾对我提到，你看，像明尼阿波利斯的德里克·肖万案，

sentences.en: where you had a racially diverse jury, and the case went against Mr. Chauvin, the white police officer.
sentences.zh: 那里的陪审团种族多元，结果案件对白人警察肖万不利。

sentences.en: Back in 2013, you had the case of George Zimmerman, the neighborhood watch guy who had shot and killed an African-American teenager, Trayvon Martin.
sentences.zh: 早在2013年，乔治·齐默尔曼案中，这位社区巡逻员枪杀了非裔美国少年特雷沃恩·马丁。

sentences.en: When he went to trial, he was acquitted, and that was a largely white jury.
sentences.zh: 当他受审时，他被判无罪，那是一个以白人为主的陪审团。

sentences.en: So this was an extremely important moment in this drama when that jury was finally seated.
sentences.zh: 所以，当陪审团最终落座时，这是这场戏剧中极其重要的时刻。

sentences.en: And Richard, do we have any actual evidence that not really talking about race was a strategy from this prosecutor tailored to this jury?
sentences.zh: 理查德，我们有什么确凿证据表明不谈种族问题是这位检察官为该陪审团量身定制的策略吗？

sentences.en: Well, Ms. Dino Koski and her team haven't talked about the strategy itself.
sentences.zh: 嗯，杜尼科斯基女士和她的团队并没有谈论过策略本身。

sentences.en: But from pretrial hearings and pretrial motions, we got a sense of the kind of evidence that they potentially had at their disposal
sentences.zh: 但从审前听证会和审前动议中，我们了解到他们可能掌握的证据类型，

sentences.en: that might underscore an argument that racial animus was the motive for these acts.
sentences.zh: 这些证据本可以强化“种族仇恨是这些行为动机”的论点。

sentences.en: And I think we can deduce quite a bit from the fact that none of that evidence ended up being introduced to the jury at trial.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们可以从这些证据最终都没有在审判中提交给陪审团这一事实中推断出很多东西。

sentences.en: These elements of evidence fell into three kind of buckets.
sentences.zh: 这些证据要素大致分为三类。

sentences.en: The first one was a series of what the prosecution called racial text messages and or social media postings by the three men,
sentences.zh: 第一类是检方所称的这三名男子发送的一系列种族主义短信和/或社交媒体帖子，

sentences.en: one of which we heard about a little bit in a hearing racist joke from one of the defendants to one of their friends.
sentences.zh: 其中一个我们在听证会上听到过一点，是其中一名被告发给朋友的种族主义笑话。

sentences.en: The second category was extremely explosive.
sentences.zh: 第二类极其具有爆炸性。

sentences.en: This was an allegation that the defendant Roddy Bryan had made in a conversation with the Georgia Bureau of Investigation that another defendant, Travis McMichael,
sentences.zh: 这是一项指控，被告罗迪·布莱恩在与佐治亚州调查局的谈话中称，另一名被告特拉维斯·麦克迈克尔，

sentences.en: the man who pulled the trigger of his shotgun and killed Ahmaud Arbery, had used a tremendously crude racial epithet right after the moment that he pulled the trigger.
sentences.zh: 那个扣动猎枪扳机杀害阿莫德·阿伯里的人，在扣动扳机后立即使用了极其粗俗的种族歧视用语。

sentences.en: Now, this is an allegation that Travis McMichael's lawyers said never happened.
sentences.zh: 现在，特拉维斯·麦克迈克尔的律师称这从未发生过。

sentences.en: It also would have faced just technical and legal issues and being brought to court.
sentences.zh: 如果提交法庭，它也会面临技术和法律上的问题。

sentences.en: There was a third category, though, that the judge ruled that Ms. Dunikoski was allowed to bring up in court, and she never did.
sentences.zh: 不过，还有第三类证据，法官裁定杜尼科斯基女士可以在法庭上提出，但她从未这样做。

sentences.en: And that was the presence of a decorative license plate on the front of Travis McMichael's pickup truck, the pickup truck that he and his father used
sentences.zh: 那就是特拉维斯·麦克迈克尔皮卡车前部装饰性车牌的存在，那辆他和父亲用来

sentences.en: to chase this unarmed black man through their neighborhood.
sentences.zh: 在社区里追逐这名手无寸铁的黑人男子的皮卡车。

sentences.en: It was a license plate of the old Georgia state flag, which has embedded in it the old Confederate battle flag.
sentences.zh: 那是一块旧佐治亚州州旗的车牌，上面嵌入了旧邦联战旗。

sentences.en: The defense had argued, hoping to keep the photographic evidence of this license plate out of the trial.
sentences.zh: 辩方曾辩称，希望将这张车牌的照片证据排除在审判之外。

sentences.en: But the judge ruled that Ms. Dunikoski could use it, and she didn't.
sentences.zh: 但法官裁定杜尼科斯基女士可以使用它，而她没有用。

sentences.en: So there were obviously some decisions that were being made there about holding back to a certain extent.
sentences.zh: 所以很明显，他们在某些方面做出了一些克制的决定。

sentences.en: And Richard, what would be the case that you might imagine for omitting the Confederate flag that one of these defendants had on the front of his car?
sentences.zh: 理查德，你认为省略掉其中一名被告车前悬挂的邦联旗帜，可能会是什么理由？

sentences.en: Well, you know, that old Georgia flag and this kind of decorative license plate that's in the style of the old flag is one that you see all over the state of Georgia.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道，那面旧佐治亚州旗和这种旧旗风格的装饰性车牌在佐治亚州随处可见。

sentences.en: And it's just not a super rare thing.
sentences.zh: 这并不是什么稀罕事。

sentences.en: So although we don't know what Ms. Dunikoski was thinking and the prosecution team was thinking, I think, you know, we can guess that they're sitting around before trial saying,
sentences.zh: 所以虽然我们不知道杜尼科斯基女士和检方团队在想什么，但我认为，你知道，我们可以猜测他们在审判前坐在一起讨论说：

sentences.en: well, we've got 11 white people in this jury.
sentences.zh: “好吧，我们的陪审团里有11个白人。”

sentences.en: How many of them have that license plate?
sentences.zh: “他们中有多少人有那种车牌？”

sentences.en: Or know people or just have very complicated feelings about it that, you know, might not be very widespread in Connecticut or New York, but might be in the Deep South.
sentences.zh: “或者认识有这种车牌的人，或者只是对它有非常复杂的情感，这种情感在康涅狄格州或纽约可能并不普遍，但在南方腹地却可能存在。”

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: So how do we see this strategy play out?
sentences.zh: 那么我们是如何看到这一策略发挥作用的呢？

sentences.en: Good morning, ladies and gentlemen.
sentences.zh: 早上好，女士们，先生们。

sentences.en: In the trial itself, starting with her opening argument.
sentences.zh: 在审判本身中，从她的开场陈词开始。

sentences.en: Who are we talking about in this case?
sentences.zh: 我们在这个案子里谈论的是谁？

sentences.en: Well, we were all wondering.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们都在想。

sentences.en: Well, this is 25-year-old Ahmaud Arbery.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这是25岁的阿莫德·阿伯里。

sentences.en: As she began.
sentences.zh: 当她开始时。

sentences.en: He was also a brother.
sentences.zh: 他也是一个兄弟。

sentences.en: He was an uncle.
sentences.zh: 他是一个侄子。

sentences.en: And he was an avid runner.
sentences.zh: 他是一个狂热的跑步者。

sentences.en: How she was going to handle the race issue.
sentences.zh: 她将如何处理种族问题。

sentences.en: So, ladies and gentlemen, who else do we have?
sentences.zh: 那么，女士们，先生们，我们还有谁？

sentences.en: And I'm going to be frank.
sentences.zh: 我坦率地说。

sentences.en: I thought she was going to bring it up then.
sentences.zh: 我以为她那时会提出来。

sentences.en: We have Travis McMichael seated right over here.
sentences.zh: 我们有特拉维斯·麦克迈克尔坐在正对面。

sentences.en: 34 years old at the time.
sentences.zh: 当时34岁。

sentences.en: And she absolutely did not.
sentences.zh: 但她绝对没有提。

sentences.en: Why are we here?
sentences.zh: 我们为什么会在这里？

sentences.en: We are here because of assumptions and driveway decisions.
sentences.zh: 我们在这里是因为假设和车道上的决定。

sentences.en: She really framed her opening argument around the central idea that these three men had made what Ms. Dunikoski called assumptions and driveway decisions.
sentences.zh: 她确实围绕着一个核心理念构建了她的开场陈词，即这三名男子做出了杜尼科斯基女士所说的“假设”和“车道上的决定”。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: This is the thing.
sentences.zh: 就是这个。

sentences.en: Greg McMichael is in front of 2.30 Satilla Drive.
sentences.zh: 格雷格·麦克迈克尔在萨蒂拉大道230号前。

sentences.en: He's all alone.
sentences.zh: 他独自一人。

sentences.en: And he sees Mr. Arbery running really, really fast down the street.
sentences.zh: 他看到阿伯里先生在街上跑得非常非常快。

sentences.en: He actually uses the words, hauling ass.
sentences.zh: 他实际上用了“拼命奔跑”这个词。

sentences.en: And she laid out, moment by moment, what those decisions were.
sentences.zh: 她逐一列举了那些决定是什么。

sentences.en: Where Greg McMichael sees him, and Greg McMichael makes his driveway decision to run inside his house and get his son, get his handgun,
sentences.zh: 格雷格·麦克迈克尔在哪里看到他，以及格雷格·麦克迈克尔做出了他的“车道决定”，跑进屋里叫上儿子，拿上手枪，

sentences.en: and have his son get that Remington pump shot belt.
sentences.zh: 并让他的儿子拿上那把雷明顿泵动式霰弹枪。

sentences.en: But to me, what was really interesting was the other element of that construction, which was assumptions.
sentences.zh: 但对我来说，真正有趣的是这种构建的另一个要素，即“假设”。

sentences.en: This is what he tells the police two hours or so later at the Glen County Police Station.
sentences.zh: 这是他大约两小时后在格林县警察局告诉警察的话。

sentences.en: So I thought, well, you know, he's running from somebody.
sentences.zh: “所以我心想，好吧，你知道，他在躲避某人。”

sentences.en: He's just done something.
sentences.zh: “他刚做了什么事。”

sentences.en: You know, he might have hurt somebody or whatever because, you know...
sentences.zh: “你知道，他可能伤害了某人或者别的什么，因为，你知道……”

sentences.en: And I think that word carried a lot of weight.
sentences.zh: 我认为这个词很有分量。

sentences.en: He's assumed the worst and has absolutely no immediate knowledge of any crime whatsoever.
sentences.zh: 他做出了最坏的假设，却对任何犯罪行为完全没有直接了解。

sentences.en: I think you can read the word assumption in the context of a Deep South murder trial like this as potentially signaling to a jury like this
sentences.zh: 我认为你可以将“假设”一词在像这样一场南方腹地的谋杀案审判中解读为，可能是在向这样的陪审团发出信号：

sentences.en: that the assumption was, okay, blackmail, therefore up to no good.
sentences.zh: 假设就是：好吧，黑人，所以没干好事。

sentences.en: All three of these defendants did everything they did based on assumptions,
sentences.zh: 这三名被告所做的一切都是基于假设，

sentences.en: not on facts, not on evidence, on assumptions that took a young man's life.
sentences.zh: 不是基于事实，不是基于证据，而是基于夺走了一个年轻人生命的假设。

sentences.en: And that is why we are here.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们为什么在这里的原因。

sentences.en: So she's not explicitly pointing to race as part of the assumptions that were made here.
sentences.zh: 所以她并没有明确指出种族是这里所做假设的一部分。

sentences.en: It's all implied.
sentences.zh: 一切都是暗示。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I understand we are ready to proceed with the evidence from the state.
sentences.zh: 我明白，我们准备好继续提交来自检方的证据了。

sentences.en: So Ms. Dunikoski calls a number of witnesses to the stand, many of them law enforcement.
sentences.zh: 于是杜尼科斯基女士传唤了多名证人出庭，其中许多是执法人员。

sentences.en: And we begin to see where she's going to be making some of her big points and how she's going to be making them.
sentences.zh: 我们开始看到她将在哪里提出一些重点，以及她将如何提出这些重点。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So what we're going to do right now, Detective Marcy, is we're going to go through what Greg McMichael said about what Greg McMichael did on February 23rd, 2020.
sentences.zh: 那么我们现在要做的是，马西警探，我们要梳理一下格雷格·麦克迈克尔关于他在2020年2月23日所做的事情的陈述。

sentences.en: Yes, ma'am.
sentences.zh: 是的，女士。

sentences.en: One of them is this evidence that really shows that these guys had been quite aggressive over the course of this kind of five or six minutes
sentences.zh: 其中之一是这些证据，真正表明这些家伙在这一过程中表现得相当激进，在这大约五六分钟的时间里，

sentences.en: where this chase of this unarmed man plays out in their neighborhood.

sentences.zh: 她提出的这些问题，实际上削弱了阿莫德·阿伯里对他构成严重威胁的说法。

sentences.en: And at this point in time, when you first see him on Burford, he's not reaching into his pockets?
sentences.zh: 在伯福德路第一次见到他时，他没有把手伸进口袋吧？

sentences.en: No, ma'am.
sentences.zh: 没有，女士。

sentences.en: Not running, no ma'am.
sentences.zh: 没有在跑吧，没有，女士。

sentences.en: And he never yelled at you guys?
sentences.zh: 他从来没有对你们大喊大叫吧？

sentences.en: No, ma'am.
sentences.zh: 没有，女士。

sentences.en: Never threatened you at all?
sentences.zh: 从来没有威胁过你们吧？

sentences.en: No, ma'am.
sentences.zh: 没有，女士。

sentences.en: Never brandished any weapons?
sentences.zh: 从来没有挥舞过任何武器吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, he did not threaten me verbally, no ma'am.
sentences.zh: 是的，他没有口头威胁我，没有，女士。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Didn't pull out any guns?
sentences.zh: 没有掏出过任何枪支吧？

sentences.en: No, ma'am.
sentences.zh: 没有，女士。

sentences.en: Didn't pull out any knife?
sentences.zh: 没有掏出过任何刀具吧？

sentences.en: No, ma'am.
sentences.zh: 没有，女士。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Never reached for anything, did he?
sentences.zh: 他从来没有伸手去拿什么东西，对吧？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没有。

sentences.en: He just ran?
sentences.zh: 他只是在跑？

sentences.en: Yes, he was just running.
sentences.zh: 是的，他只是在跑。

sentences.en: And she brings up the fact that Travis McMichael had been asked about whether or not Ahmaud Arbery had grabbed his gun.
sentences.zh: 她还提到了特拉维斯·麦克迈克尔曾被问及阿莫德·阿伯里是否抓住了他的枪。

sentences.en: In an interview that Travis McMichael gave to law enforcement shortly after the shooting happened.
sentences.zh: 在枪击事件发生后不久，特拉维斯·麦克迈克尔接受执法部门采访时。

sentences.en: And in that interview, he said he really wasn't sure what happened, whether the gun had been grabbed or not.
sentences.zh: 在那次采访中，他说他真的不确定发生了什么，不知道枪是否被抓住了。

sentences.en: Detective Nohilly specifically asked you, do you remember if he grabbed the shotgun at all?
sentences.zh: 诺希利警探特别问过你，你记得他有没有抓住猎枪吗？

sentences.en: And your response was, I want to say he did, but honestly, I cannot remember.
sentences.zh: 你的回答是，我想说他抓住了，但老实说，我记不清了。

sentences.en: I mean, we were, me and him were face to face the entire time.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我和他全程面对面。

sentences.en: Do you remember saying that?
sentences.zh: 你记得说过那句话吗？

sentences.en: Yes, and I was trying to think of that exact moment.
sentences.zh: 是的，我当时正试图回想那一刻。

sentences.en: He had the weapon the way that I was describing it.
sentences.zh: 他确实像我描述的那样拿着武器。

sentences.en: But why I said he did not have the gun at that second, I don't know why.
sentences.zh: 但为什么我说那一秒他没拿枪，我不知道为什么。

sentences.en: But it happened so fast and trying to recall and everything, I've obviously missed every minute detail.
sentences.zh: 但事情发生得太快了，试图回忆一切，我显然漏掉了每一个微小的细节。

sentences.en: So that is inconsistent with what he has just said on the stand.
sentences.zh: 所以这与他刚才在证人席上所说的不一致。

sentences.en: Yeah, inconsistent and ostensibly harmful.
sentences.zh: 是的，不一致，而且表面上是有害的。

sentences.en: In the eyes of the jury.
sentences.zh: 在陪审团眼中。

sentences.en: So what we see in the cross-examination of Travis McMichael is this prosecutor, Ms. Dunikoski,
sentences.zh: 所以我们在对特拉维斯·麦克迈克尔的交叉盘问中看到，这位检察官杜尼科斯基女士，

sentences.en: really working to dismantle the argument of the defense that Travis McMichael had acted in self-defense.
sentences.zh: 正在努力拆解辩方关于特拉维斯·麦克迈克尔是正当防卫的论点。

sentences.en: But isn't it true that Satilla Shores only had one burglary call in all of 2019 and it was a false alarm?
sentences.zh: 但萨蒂拉海岸在2019年全年只有一个入室盗窃报警电话，而且还是误报，这不是事实吗？

sentences.en: We see her dismantling the idea that he had acted in the spirit of the citizen's arrest law.
sentences.zh: 我们看到她拆解了他是在公民逮捕法精神下行事的观点。

sentences.en: And then seeing a burglary on the Facebook page, that was what that I was heard about the neighborhood.
sentences.zh: 然后在Facebook页面上看到入室盗窃的消息，那就是我听到的关于社区的情况。

sentences.en: So you're telling this jury that what you heard was rumor from other people?
sentences.zh: 所以你是告诉陪审团，你听到的只是别人的传言？

sentences.en: It was what I was told from my mother and seeing on Facebook and from the neighbors.
sentences.zh: 这是我从母亲那里听说的，也是在Facebook上看到的，还是从邻居那里听来的。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So you don't know this from the police, that's correct.
sentences.zh: 所以你并不是从警方那里得知此事的，没错吧。

sentences.en: I didn't hear it from the police, no.
sentences.zh: 我不是从警方那里听说的，没有。

sentences.en: The information, it turns out, that he had about this guy turned out to be not very firm and not really from the best sources.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，他掌握的关于这个人的信息并不确凿，来源也不是最好的。

sentences.en: And again, these were the two pillars of the defense's argument.
sentences.zh: 再说一次，这些是辩方论点的两大支柱。

sentences.en: And we're really seeing the way the prosecution is now trying to take those apart.
sentences.zh: 我们现在确实看到了检方正试图如何拆解这些论点。

sentences.en: So here again, the prosecutor is turning to this idea of assumptions, which of course are not the legal basis for arresting someone or shooting them.
sentences.zh: 所以在这里，检察官再次转向了“假设”这一概念，当然，这并不是逮捕某人或射杀某人的法律依据。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's her argument.
sentences.zh: 是的，那是她的论点。

sentences.en: And we're going to see in her closing arguments for the first time, this explicit argument that these crimes had been committed with a racial motive.
sentences.zh: 我们将在她的结案陈词中首次看到这种明确的论点，即这些罪行是出于种族动机而犯下的。

sentences.en: And she does so with this one sentence where she says that Mr. Arbery was attacked.
sentences.zh: 她用一句话做到了这一点，她说阿伯里先生遭到了袭击。

sentences.en: Because he was a black man running down the street.
sentences.zh: 因为他是一个在街上奔跑的黑人。

sentences.en: Because he was a black man running down the street.
sentences.zh: 因为他是一个在街上奔跑的黑人。

sentences.en: But the bottom line is, but for their actions, but for their decisions, but for their choices, Ahmaud Arbery would be alive.
sentences.zh: 但归根结底，如果不是因为他们的行为，如果不是因为他们的决定，如果不是因为他们的选择，阿莫德·阿伯里现在还活着。

sentences.en: But still, what she really focuses so much of her closing arguments and then her subsequent rebuttal on was not this kind of idea where race is central to the argument.
sentences.zh: 但尽管如此，她在结案陈词以及随后的反驳中所真正关注的，并不是这种将种族作为论点核心的想法。

sentences.en: Don't chase down strangers to confront them.
sentences.zh: 不要追赶陌生人去与他们对质。

sentences.en: Don't go after pedestrians in your truck.
sentences.zh: 不要开着卡车去追赶行人。

sentences.en: But this idea that these guys had just been really stupid, that they had really kind of acted in a way that would just sort of defied all common sense.
sentences.zh: 而是这种想法，即这些人真的太愚蠢了，他们的行为简直违背了所有常识。

sentences.en: I mean, common sense tells you, you pull up in a truck on somebody who's like a pedestrian who's out for a job.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，常识告诉你，你不能开着卡车冲向一个正在慢跑的行人。

sentences.en: I mean, I don't know, are any of you runners?
sentences.zh: 我是说，我不知道，你们中间有人跑步吗？

sentences.en: You ever had a strange truck pull up and have some people start yelling at you?
sentences.zh: 你们有没有遇到过陌生的卡车停下来，有人开始对你们大喊大叫？

sentences.en: At one point, she says to them,
sentences.zh: 在某一时刻，她对他们说，

sentences.en: Don't go looking for trouble.
sentences.zh: 不要去自找麻烦。

sentences.en: Don't go looking for trouble.
sentences.zh: 不要去自找麻烦。

sentences.en: Because you will find it, and it is not going to turn out the way you think it is.
sentences.zh: 因为你会找到麻烦的，而且结果不会像你想象的那样。

sentences.en: And what about the defense?
sentences.zh: 那么辩方呢？

sentences.en: How do they make their closing argument here?
sentences.zh: 他们在这里是如何进行结案陈词的？

sentences.en: The most noteworthy of the closing arguments came from Laura Hogue, who's a veteran criminal defense attorney out of Macon, Georgia.
sentences.zh: 最值得注意的结案陈词来自劳拉·霍格，她是佐治亚州梅肯市的一位资深刑事辩护律师。

sentences.en: And it was Ms. Hogue who made what ended up being perhaps the most talked about comments in this case.
sentences.zh: 正是霍格女士发表了本案中或许最受议论的评论。

sentences.en: Turning Ahmaud Arbery into a victim after the choices that he made does not reflect the reality of what brought Ahmaud Arbery to Satilla Shores in his khaki shorts with no socks to cover his long,
sentences.zh: 在阿莫德·阿伯里做出那些选择后，将他塑造成受害者，并不能反映他穿着卡其色短裤、没穿袜子、露出长长……

sentences.en: dirty toenails.
sentences.zh: 脏脚趾甲来到萨蒂拉海岸的真实情况。

sentences.en: She's making this case that Ahmaud Arbery should not be considered a victim.
sentences.zh: 她提出的观点是，阿莫德·阿伯里不应被视为受害者。

sentences.en: He was a recurring nighttime intruder.
sentences.zh: 他是一个反复出现的夜间入侵者。

sentences.en: And that is frightening and unsettling.
sentences.zh: 这令人恐惧且不安。

sentences.en: He died because for whatever inexplicable, illogical reason, instead of staying where he was,
sentences.zh: 他之所以死亡，是因为出于某种无法解释、不合逻辑的原因，他没有留在原地，

sentences.en: whatever overwhelming reason he had to avoid being captured that day and arrested by the police,
sentences.zh: 出于某种无法抗拒的原因，他那天要避免被抓获并被警察逮捕，

sentences.en: he chose to fight.
sentences.zh: 他选择了反抗。

sentences.en: He chose to fight.
sentences.zh: 他选择了反抗。

sentences.en: It was the first time we saw so explicitly a portrait painted of Ahmaud Arbery as someone who should be so feared.
sentences.zh: 这是我们第一次如此明确地看到阿莫德·阿伯里被描绘成一个应该让人如此恐惧的人。

sentences.en: I realize probably more than any of you what an incredibly unpopular thing that is to say.
sentences.zh: 我意识到，这番话有多么不受欢迎，我可能比你们任何人都清楚。

sentences.en: Somebody's got to say it.
sentences.zh: 总得有人说出来。

sentences.en: And believe me, I'm proud to be the one to say it.
sentences.zh: 相信我，我很自豪能成为说出这句话的人。

sentences.en: And Richard, what do you make of the decision by the defense to go there?
sentences.zh: 理查德，你如何看待辩方决定走这一步？

sentences.en: Is this a sign of desperation?
sentences.zh: 这是绝望的迹象吗？

sentences.en: A reflection of the fact that the prosecution has done such a compelling job of making the case that there was no crime here to justify a citizen's arrest or a threat sufficient enough to justify shooting under self-defense?
sentences.zh: 这是否反映出检方已经非常有说服力地证明了这里不存在任何犯罪行为，不足以证明公民逮捕的合理性，也不足以证明在自卫下射杀的合理性？

sentences.en: And therefore, perhaps the defense sees this as their last possible hope to basically appeal to the biases and fears of this mostly white jury?
sentences.zh: 因此，辩方是否认为这是他们最后的希望，基本上是在诉诸这个以白人为主的陪审团的偏见和恐惧？

sentences.en: Well, again, there are a lot of people watching this case who felt like the defense's argument from the very beginning, talking about duty and responsibility, etc.,
sentences.zh: 嗯，再说一次，有很多关注此案的人认为，辩方从一开始就谈论义务和责任等的论点，

sentences.en: were making this implicitly a story about race.
sentences.zh: 是在含蓄地讲述一个关于种族的故事。

sentences.en: And when Laura Hogue makes this case in her closing argument,
sentences.zh: 当劳拉·霍格在结案陈词中提出这一观点时，

sentences.en: there was a feeling among a lot of people that this was just moving right up to the line of making it explicitly about race.
sentences.zh: 很多人感觉到这已经触及了明确讨论种族问题的底线。

sentences.en: Not exactly, because she never uses these words like black and white, but it felt like that sort of implicit argument was strengthened.
sentences.zh: 不完全是，因为她从未使用过“黑人”和“白人”这样的词，但感觉那种含蓄的论点被加强了。

sentences.en: And of course, a lot of people were really horrified by this language about Ahmaud Arbery's dirty toenails.
sentences.zh: 当然，很多人对关于阿莫德·阿伯里脏脚趾甲的言论感到非常震惊。

sentences.en: To a lot of people, it felt like race-baiting.
sentences.zh: 对许多人来说，这感觉像是种族诱导。

sentences.en: To a lot of people, it felt very raciSt.
sentences.zh: 对许多人来说，这感觉非常种族主义。

sentences.en: So I was really interested in why Laura Hogue would have made these comments about the toenails.
sentences.zh: 所以我真的很想知道劳拉·霍格为什么要发表关于脚趾甲的评论。

sentences.en: I reached out to her law partner and husband, Frank Hogue,
sentences.zh: 我联系了她的合伙人兼丈夫弗兰克·霍格，

sentences.en: and he essentially talked about how important it is for a defense attorney in a murder case to give a full-throated and zealous defense of their client.
sentences.zh: 他基本上谈到了刑事辩护律师在谋杀案中为客户进行全力以赴的辩护是多么重要。

sentences.en: Anything less is just not doing the job of a criminal defense attorney.
sentences.zh: 任何少于此的做法都不能算是一个合格的刑事辩护律师。

sentences.en: And their sense of why the toenails comment was important and needed to be added, according to him,
sentences.zh: 据他说，他们认为脚趾甲的评论之所以重要且有必要加入，

sentences.en: was they felt like they really needed to push back against this narrative that Ahmaud Arbery was a jogger in the neighborhood that day.
sentences.zh: 是因为他们觉得真的需要反驳那天阿莫德·阿伯里只是在社区慢跑的说法。

sentences.en: I know from my reporting that Ahmaud Arbery was a runner.
sentences.zh: 我从我的报道中得知，阿莫德·阿伯里是一名跑步者。

sentences.en: I talked to people in neighborhoods and in businesses in that area who told me that they saw him running all the time.
sentences.zh: 我与该地区的居民和商家交谈过，他们告诉我经常看到他在跑步。

sentences.en: There is a question about whether or not he jogged into that neighborhood on that particular day.
sentences.zh: 关于他那天是否慢跑进入那个社区，确实存在疑问。

sentences.en: But the Hoag's felt like bringing up this detail about the dirty toenails would really serve as a powerful and effective pushback against the idea that it was really jogging that Ahmaud Arbery was up to that day.
sentences.zh: 但霍格夫妇认为，提出关于脏脚趾甲的细节，将是对阿莫德·阿伯里那天是在慢跑这一想法的有力且有效的反击。

sentences.en: And for me, it raises this kind of question of what we think of as a jogger, which I think it's a pastime or a hobby or a sport or whatever,
sentences.zh: 对我来说，这引发了一个关于我们如何定义“慢跑者”的问题，我认为这是一种消遣、爱好、运动或其他什么，

sentences.en: that I think carries with it a lot of assumptions and a lot of, you know, kind of class baggage.
sentences.zh: 我认为它带有许多假设和许多，你知道，某种阶级包袱。

sentences.en: Ahmaud Arbery was not a rich guy.
sentences.zh: 阿莫德·阿伯里不是个有钱人。

sentences.en: One of the reasons he ran, I think, is because it was the kind of most reliable way for a guy without a lot of money to get around.
sentences.zh: 我认为他跑步的原因之一，是因为对于一个没有多少钱的人来说，这是最可靠的出行方式。

sentences.en: And I think we can ask the question about whether or not Frank and Laura Hoag, who are two highly respected criminal defense attorneys,
sentences.zh: 我想我们可以问一个问题，弗兰克和劳拉·霍格这两位备受尊敬的刑事辩护律师，

sentences.en: knew that they were raising the issue of race and trying to play to the perceived racist perceptions of jurors and talking about Ahmaud Arbery's body in that way.
sentences.zh: 是否知道他们提出了种族问题，并试图利用陪审员心中潜在的种族主义偏见，以那种方式谈论阿莫德·阿伯里的身体。

sentences.en: Well, whatever the intent, we know it didn't really work for the defense.
sentences.zh: 嗯，无论意图如何，我们知道这对辩方并没有真正起作用。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think it's fair to assume that.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为这样假设是公平的。

sentences.en: Soon after, this nearly all-white jury moved very quickly in arriving at a verdict, and they found all three of these men guilty of murder.
sentences.zh: 不久之后，这个几乎全是白人的陪审团非常迅速地达成了裁决，他们认定这三名男子谋杀罪名成立。

sentences.en: And how about the strategy, Richard, that did work, in which the prosecution decided not to claim that race was the major motivation in this case?
sentences.zh: 那么理查德，那个奏效的策略呢？检方决定不声称种族是本案的主要动机。

sentences.en: I wonder if there was any discomfort among Ahmaud Arbery's family or among Black leaders in Georgia that this winning strategy ultimately did downplay race.
sentences.zh: 我想知道阿莫德·阿伯里的家人或佐治亚州的黑人领袖是否对这一获胜策略最终淡化了种族问题感到不安。

sentences.en: Well, you'll remember that lots of people were skeptical and critical of this strategy,
sentences.zh: 嗯，你会记得很多人对这一策略持怀疑和批评态度，

sentences.en: and they were concerned about the idea of not knitting together a narrative with race as the motive.
sentences.zh: 他们担心不把种族作为动机来编织叙事这一想法。

sentences.en: And they were worried about the moral implications, I think, of not making race central to this version of events.
sentences.zh: 我认为，他们担心不把种族作为这一事件版本的核心所带来的道德影响。

sentences.en: But Ahmaud Arbery's family was extremely pleased with the way Ms. Dunikoski conducted herself in court before there was even a verdict.
sentences.zh: 但阿莫德·阿伯里的家人对杜尼科斯基女士在法庭上的表现感到非常满意，甚至在裁决出来之前就是如此。

sentences.en: And from other conversations with African American people in Brunswick, Georgia, after the verdict, you got this sense that for a lot of people,
sentences.zh: 从裁决后与佐治亚州布伦瑞克市非裔美国人的其他谈话中，你会感觉到对许多人来说，

sentences.en: it felt like a more poignant victory based on the fact that it really came down largely to the question of whether these guys were wrong in doing what they did.
sentences.zh: 这感觉是一场更令人心酸的胜利，因为事实归根结底很大程度上在于这些人所做的事情是否错误。

sentences.en: And that leaving the case to be tried on those grounds without the kind of extensive racial baggage around it was in some ways an even more powerful statement to make.
sentences.zh: 而让案件在这些基础上进行审判，而不带有周围那种广泛的种族包袱，在某种程度上是一个更有力的声明。

sentences.en: Well, Richard, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 好的，理查德，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: We appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我们很感激。

sentences.en: Thank you, Michael.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，迈克尔。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要知道的其他消息。

sentences.en: Over the weekend,
sentences.zh: 周末期间，

sentences.en: many countries introduced new travel restrictions to limit the spread of a troubling new variant of the coronavirus that was first detected in South Africa and Botswana.
sentences.zh: 许多国家出台了新的旅行限制措施，以限制一种令人担忧的新冠病毒新变种的传播，该变种最早在南非和博茨瓦纳被发现。

sentences.en: The variant, named Omicron, has been reported in at least a dozen countries, including Britain, Australia, and Denmark.
sentences.zh: 这种名为奥密克戎的变种已在至少十几个国家被报告，包括英国、澳大利亚和丹麦。

sentences.en: That has prompted governments, including the U.S.
sentences.zh: 这促使包括美国在内的各国政府，

sentences.en: and Canada, to temporarily ban most travelers from countries across Southern Africa.
sentences.zh: 和加拿大，暂时禁止了来自南部非洲各国的大多数旅客入境。

sentences.en: Much is still unknown about the variant, but experts like Dr. Anthony Fauci fear that based on the mutations they've studied so far, Omicron could be highly contagious.
sentences.zh: 关于该变种还有很多未知之处，但像安东尼·福奇博士这样的专家担心，根据他们目前研究的突变情况，奥密克戎可能具有高度传染性。

sentences.en: The profile of the mutation strongly suggests that it's going to have an advantage in transmissibility and that it might evade immune protection that you would get, for example,
sentences.zh: 突变的特征强烈表明它在传播性方面将具有优势，并且它可能会逃避你所获得的免疫保护，例如，

sentences.en: from a monoclonal antibody or from the convalescent serum after a person's been infected and possibly even against some of the vaccine-induced antibodies.
sentences.zh: 来自单克隆抗体或人感染后的恢复期血清，甚至可能对抗一些疫苗诱导的抗体。

sentences.en: In an interview on Sunday with NBC News, Fauci said that the best protection against the variant remains vaccinations and booster shots.
sentences.zh: 在周日接受NBC新闻采访时，福奇表示，针对该变种的最佳保护仍然是接种疫苗和加强针。

sentences.en: Even with variants like Omicron, if you get boosted,
sentences.zh: 即使对于像奥密克戎这样的变种，如果你接种了加强针，

sentences.en: you're going to get a level of antibody that's high enough that it is likely you'll be able to get at least some degree and maybe a lot of protection against this.
sentences.zh: 你将获得足够高的抗体水平，很可能至少能获得一定程度，甚至可能是很大程度的针对该变种的保护。

sentences.en: The Omicron variant will be the subject of tomorrow's show.
sentences.zh: 奥密克戎变种将是明天节目的主题。

sentences.zh: 这就是《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.zh: 本周在《Wirecutter秀》中，我们正在为假期招待客人做准备。

sentences.en: Tune in for tips on making your guests feel at home.
sentences.zh: 敬请收听，获取让客人感到宾至如归的建议。

sentences.en: Are they a blackout sleeper?
sentences.zh: 他们是需要完全黑暗才能睡觉的人吗？

sentences.en: I don't mean do they blackout to go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我不是指他们是否会昏睡过去。

sentences.en: I mean, what kind of light do they require?
sentences.zh: 我是指，他们需要什么样的光线？

sentences.en: Because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 因为那是一件非常具体的事情。

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 他们有过敏症或食物敏感吗？

sentences.en: Are they coffee tea drinkers?
sentences.zh: 他们是喝咖啡还是喝茶的人？

sentences.en: What time do they like to get up?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢几点起床？
